children: Netflix cuts ~6% of workforce (~1,000 jobs), mainly in product, tech, legal and HR. Layoff notice came Oct 14 ahead of Oct 20 earnings (Q3 revenue $12.86B; EPS $0.82).
Netflix (NFLX) sees Q3 revenue growth ~12%, narrows 2026 revenue outlook to $51.0–$51.4B and projects 2026 full-year growth of 13%–14%, down from 16.5% in 2025 due to slower subscriber gains
Netflix (NFLX) Q3 U.S. churn rose 16.6% YoY and 8.5% QoQ, the largest quarterly churn jump so far; U.S./North America engagement lagged other regions.
Netflix says content spending will rise ~10% this year and is cutting back-office and tech staff. It added an ad tier, live programming and gaming to boost revenue alongside subscriptions.
Huber Research cut Netflix (NFLX) to Underweight and trimmed its price target to $70 from $85, citing weak audience engagement, possible job cuts, and change to annual viewership reporting from 2027.
Netflix (NFLX) reports falling viewing time and weaker user engagement. Traders note rising competition from YouTube and TikTok and analyst comments on engagement trends affecting stock performance.
NFLX shares down >40% year-on-year as user growth slows. Company adding sports, podcasts and creator shows to boost engagement; shifting select films to theatrical release, including 2027 Narnia.
Netflix (NFLX) lost bid for Warner Bros. Discovery studio and streaming assets, won by Paramount Skydance in ~ $110B deal; report notes this amid recent Netflix layoffs.
